items.title: PM announces new powers to boost fuel supply amid Middle East tensions
items.description: The Albanese government will use public money to underwrite the delivery of extra cargoes of fuel in a bid to shore up supply during the Middle East conflict.

items.title: 'Got it all wrong': The miscalculation the US and Israel made over Iran
items.description: Donald Trump is deploying thousands of marines and extra battleships to the Middle East, while also claiming to be close to a deal with Iran to end the war. So is he set to wind down his war with Iran, or is he thinking of escalating?

items.title: Trump under pressure to find an off-ramp amid oil and munitions crisis
items.description: While markets struggle to price a sudden collapse in oil supply, military analysts are sounding the alarm on the rate countries are burning through weapons stockpiles.

items.title: Bank of America agrees to pay $105 million to settle Epstein-related lawsuit
items.description: The Bank of America has agreed to pay $US72.5 million ($105.3 million) to settle a civil lawsuit brought by women who accused the bank of facilitating their sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein, court records show.

items.title: Hundreds owed $10,000 from Medicare as millions go unclaimed
items.description: Services Australia is urging people to check if they're owed money from a $272 million pool of unclaimed money.

items.title: Live: 'A lot of destruction': Thousands remain without power as ex-Cyclone Narelle continues south
items.description: The storm, which has already made landfall in Far North Queensland and the Northern Territory, is now impacting the WA coast.

items.title: Live: Saints and Lions take heated clash to the wire in tense last quarter
items.description: St Kilda and Brisbane have made enemies of each other off the field, which means there is plenty to play for on it as they kick off Saturday's AFL action. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Knights star confirmed to return against unbeaten Bulldogs
items.description: Newcastle have confirmed five-eighth Fletcher Sharpe will make his return from a knee injury as the Knights travel to Homebush to take on Canterbury. Follow live.

items.title: Greek villages 'becoming ghost towns' as an alarming problem takes hold
items.description: Greece's population could drop by as much as 20 per cent by 2050, with the government declaring the situation a "national threat".

items.title: Tiger Woods arrested following car crash near Florida home
items.description: Golf legend Tiger Woods is arrested in Florida after refusing to submit a urine sample following a car crash near his Florida home.

items.title: This man went viral after surviving Bondi. Then the internet took a dark turn
items.description: Arsen Ostrovsky was on the ground, bleeding, at the Bondi attack when he decided to take a selfie. Within 2 hours it was circulating on the internet. In less than a day, it had become fodder for a global conspiracy theory.

items.title: Mapping Israel's destruction of Lebanese bridges
items.description: Israel's expanded invasion of southern Lebanon was at least 12 days in the making, with bridges targeted to effectively cut off the south from the country's centre.

items.title: US 'on verge' of ending Iran war as Rubio demands allies lead postwar coalition
items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio tells G7 leaders to ready a postwar coalition to secure the Strait of Hormuz, saying the US-Israeli war on Iran could conclude within weeks.

items.title: 'Built on deception': How one online travel site is fleecing customers
items.description: As holiday-makers gear up for Easter, online travel site Guest Reservations is accused of fleecing customers using hidden fees and charges with advocates calling on government and the regulator to step in.

items.title: As music festivals collapse, one scrappy underdog is making a lot of noise
items.description: As music festivals collapse, one Geelong kid's hobby has turned into a big day out.

items.title: The nine books that knocked our critics' socks off this month
items.description: Wondering what to read next? Gothic crime fiction, a cult Japanese bestseller and a fantastical twist on the Blitz are among our critics' latest recommendations.

items.title: Newlyweds sell everything to buy 160-year-old former pub
items.description: A 160-year-old hotel sat on the market for four years, until Jason and Kyla Romaior decided to take a risk. Insurance costs are $20,000 a year, but they are confident they have what it takes to handle the challenges of owning a heritage building.

items.title: Head of TGA speaks out on sunscreen scandal
items.description: In his first interview since the sunscreen controversy erupted almost 10 months ago, the Therapeutic Goods Administration head says he hopes the proposed shake-up of regulations will restore consumer confidence.

items.title: End of an era for general store owned by family for 100 years
items.description: The Tharwa General Store — which has been run by the same family since 1926 — has been many things: a post office, a mechanic's workshop, a fuel stop, a lolly shop, a watering hole, and above all, a place where a community comes together.

items.title: Trump's new tourism envoy once proposed banishing pigeons from Sydney streets
items.description: US President Donald Trump has named Nick Adams as his new special presidential envoy for tourism. It isn't the Australian's first time in government.

items.title: 'Gigantic waves' batter NSW coastline amid 'treacherous' surf conditions
items.description: Huge swells have inundated NSW beaches as most of the coastline remains closed to the public due to hazardous surf conditions.

items.title: Remote WA area connected to outside world with first at-home internet service
items.description: Residents from remote Ngalingkadji in Western Australia's north are being connected to the internet at home for the first time, bringing banking services, telehealth and emergency services.

items.title: Australia sets record score to claim 1-0 series lead over West Indies
items.description: Australia power to a 103-run win over the West Indies, despite Stafanie Taylor's breakthrough one-day century.

items.title: Do we actually have the workforce for the $4b NDIS alternative?
items.description: Months away from the start of a huge shift in disability support for children, the workforce expected to deliver it has concerns about its readiness.

items.title: Isolated school students make sacrifices amid fuel crisis
items.description: Ruben Driver has a round trip of 4,000 kilometres to reach his boarding school. The cost of fuel is placing his family under immense pressure to get him to class.
